records.title: Unigenitus Dei Filius
records.textVerification: Not independently checked in this inventory

review.note: Automatically grouped from collection headings; document identity and completeness need review

sourceLines: [From the Bull of jubilee, "Unigenitus Dei Filius," Jan. 25, 1343] The only begotten Son of God . . . "made unto us from God, wisdom, justice, sanctification and redemption" [1 Cor. 3], "neither by the blood of goats or of calves, but by His own blood entered once into the holies having obtained eternal redemption" [Heb. 9:12]. "For not with corruptible things as gold or silver, but with the precious blood of His very (Son) as of a lamb unspotted and unstained He has redeemed us" [cf.1 Pet. 1:18-19], who innocent, immolated on the altar of the Cross is known to have poured out not a little drop of blood, which however on account of union with the Word would have been sufficient for the redemption of the whole human race, but copiously as a kind of flowing stream, so that "from the soles of His feet even to the top of His Head no soundness was found in Him" [ Is. 1:6]. Therefore, how great a treasure did the good Father acquire from this for the Church militant, so that the mercy of so great an effusion was not rendered useless, vain or superfluous, wishing to lay up treasures for His sons, so that thus the Church is an infinite treasure to men, so that they who use it, become the friends of God [ Wis. 7:14].

scope: All local entries, plus explicitly catalogued external documents. Inferred source groups are not a verified count of distinct documents.

relations.note: Lumen Gentium reiterates the irreformability of papal definitions. This identifies a shared doctrinal assertion, not a claim that every sentence in either passage is a definition.

evidence.quote: his definitions, of themselves, and not from the consent of the Church, are justly styled irreformable
such definitions of the Roman Pontiff from himself, but not from the consensus of the Church, are unalterable

relations.note: The responsum explicitly addresses the status of the teaching in Ordinatio Sacerdotalis, rather than announcing a new papal ex cathedra definition.

evidence.quote: which is presented in the Apostolic Letter Ordinatio Sacerdotalis to be held definitively
this judgment is to be definitively held by all the Church's faithful

relations.note: The responsum cites Lumen Gentium 25, paragraph 2, when explaining the ordinary and universal magisterium.

evidence.quote: cf. Second Vatican Council, Dogmatic Constitution on the Church Lumen Gentium 25, 2
they are in agreement on one position as definitively to be held

relations.note: Ministeria Quaedam expressly quotes LG 10 on the relation between the common and ministerial priesthood. Translation wording differs between these local selections.

evidence.quote: the common priesthood of the faithful and the ministerial or hierarchical priesthood, though they differ in essence and not only in degree
the common priesthood of the faithful and the ministerial or hierarchical priesthood are nonetheless interrelated

relations.note: Traditionis Custodes changes the framework for use of the 1962 Missal and abrogates incompatible prior norms. This relationship concerns discipline; it does not identify a reversal of dogma or claim every earlier norm was abrogated.

evidence.quote: Previous norms, instructions, permissions, and customs that do not conform to the provisions of the present Motu Proprio are abrogated.
For such a celebration with either Missal, the priest needs no permission from the Apostolic See or from his own Ordinary.

relations.note: The accompanying CDF letter explains the reasoning behind the 2018 Catechism revision. This relationship does not resolve the separate disputed question of continuity with earlier teaching.

evidence.quote: the increasing understanding that the dignity of a person is not lost even after committing the most serious crimes
there is an increasing awareness that the dignity of the person is not lost even after the commission of very serious crimes

relations.note: The doctrinal commentary lists papal primacy and infallibility among the truths covered by the first paragraph of the profession. This is a classification of the doctrine, not a direct citation of this Denzinger number.

evidence.quote: the doctrine on the primacy and infallibility of the Roman Pontiff
that the Roman Pontiff, when he speaks ex cathedra

roadmap.scope: The source inventory covers all local entries and explicitly catalogued external texts. It is not an exhaustive catalogue of Catholic teaching.

priorities.title: Review inherited source groups
priorities.note: Establish document identity, issuing body, translation and dates from primary sources before treating inferred groups as verified documents.

priorities.title: Complete local Vatican II texts
priorities.note: All 16 documents have official complete-text links. Eleven have local selections. The five external-only documents need reuse review and checked transcription before becoming locally searchable.

priorities.title: Preconciliar papal teaching
priorities.note: Rerum Novarum, Quas Primas, Mediator Dei and Humani Generis have source records and full-text links. Extend one pontificate and genre at a time, beginning with Leo XIII, Pius XI and Pius XII.

priorities.title: Additional papal teaching
priorities.note: Lumen Fidei, Sacramentum Caritatis, Salvifici Doloris, Vita Consecrata, Rosarium Virginis Mariae, Laudate Deum and Dilexit Nos are accessible externally; their complete texts have not been ingested.

priorities.title: Episcopal and Eastern Catholic teaching
priorities.note: Select collections with explicit jurisdiction, approval and provenance rather than attempting an undifferentiated archive.

roadmap.feedbackPolicy: No background analytics or automatic transmission of searches. Research gaps are saved only when you choose, on this browser. You can delete them or choose to open a GitHub proposal yourself. Corrections, proposals and scheduled link-check reports guide future priorities.
